requirement:
The tracked source-read operation resolves the selected `OutlineId` through
the application's source-node mapping and reads that node through `Domain`.
Successful reads delivered to the caller record that node's identity and the
fingerprint of its supplied contents.

The graph's recording and freshness contracts apply under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs` and
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test sources and did not request any implementation source.

Obligations derived from `requirements.sdk.sources.provider_observations`:
1. The tracked read resolves the selected `OutlineId` through the application's source-node mapping.
2. The tracked read reads that node through `Domain`, not from disk.
3. A successful read delivered to the caller records the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.
4. The cited graph contracts (`node_inputs`, `checking_records`) are context only and are not reassessed here. The failed-read and unmapped-id cases are covered below anyway, because they bear on the obligation to record only successful reads.

How the tests cover them:
- `agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[direct_source_reads_preserve_mapping_errors_and_record_only_successful_returns]`:
  - Mapping failures: an unknown path and an unknown selector both give an "unsupported source item" error, and `dependencies()` stays empty. The domain's `reads` count is 0 and `read_nodes` is empty, so no domain read happens when mapping fails.
  - Failed read: with `fail_read` set, the error is returned and no dependency is recorded.
  - Successful read: the returned contents are the domain's text, and `dependencies()` equals `Dependency::Node("source-node", returned.fingerprint())`. The domain's `read_nodes` is `["source-node", ...]`, which shows the read went through the mapped node.
  - Freshness: after `finish`, `is_current` is true, and it becomes false once the domain text changes. This shows the recorded fingerprint is of the supplied contents.
- `fn[fixed_tools_deliver_domain_contents_with_mandatory_snapshot_dependencies]`:
  - The `read_source` tool delivers the domain's "prepared domain contents", not the disk's "disk text".
  - Its dependency is exactly `Node("source-node", Content(...).fingerprint())`, and the domain's `read_nodes` is `["source-node"]`.
  - Rejected reads (an ignored file, `../` path, bad selectors) add no read.
  - The tool-delivered observations are recorded. Paged follow-up reads keep returning the same dependencies, even after the domain text changes, so they match the contents actually supplied.
  - Discovery tools (list, outline, search) produce no dependencies, and `domain.reads` is 0 after them.
- `fn[configured_agent_uses_domain_source_tools_in_independent_executions]`:
  - This is an end-to-end run through a model tool loop. Different source paths map to different nodes (1, 7, 8, 9), and each carries the fingerprint of the supplied content. An excluded file adds nothing, and unread files add nothing.
  - The disk contents are not delivered, and the final `verify` dependencies are asserted exactly, twice, in independent executions.
- `fn[deterministic_source_reads_reuse_saved_results]` checks the recorded `Node` dependency through `refresh_evidence`, and shows that a changed domain text yields new output.
- `agent/tests.rs` `fn[source_tools_keep_search_discovery_separate_from_delivered_source_reads]` and `fn[cached_selected_source_reads_record_exact_delivered_contents_and_errors_add_no_input]`:
  - The observation recorded is the one for the delivered contents.
  - A selected-node read records exactly the selected node's text. A read of a missing selector adds no input.
- `fn[source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads]` shows discovery and paging do not trigger observation.

Every clause is exercised with assertions on the exact recorded `Dependency` (identity and fingerprint) and on which node the domain was asked to read. The failure and unmapped boundaries are asserted too. I found no scenario in which a violating implementation would still pass these tests. Examples would be reading from disk, recording a fingerprint of different contents, recording on failure, or ignoring the mapping. All are tagged with `{test}` references to the subject. No gaps were found, and there are no acknowledgments.

The tracked source-read operation resolves the selected `OutlineId` through
the application's source-node mapping and reads that node through `Domain`.
Successful reads delivered to the caller record that node's identity and the
fingerprint of its supplied contents.
The graph's recording and freshness contracts apply under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs` and
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
:::{req} node_inputs
Finishing a verification includes every successful tracked node read in its
`Fingerprinted`, whether ordinary code or a model tool requested it. Each observation
contains the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.
A failed read returns an error without inventing a successful observation.
Repeating an identical observation adds no information. Reading the same
identity with two different fingerprints preserves both observations.
:::{req} checking_records
```rust,ignore
/// Compare each recorded input with the current domain state.
/// Return true when every fingerprint still matches, including an empty trace.
pub fn check_inputs<D: Domain, O>(
domain: &D,
inputs: &Fingerprinted<D, O>,
) -> Result<bool, D::Error>;
The function resolves the recorded dependencies through graph operations and
fingerprinting, comparing each with its saved observation. A fingerprint
mismatch returns `Ok(false)` and permits an early return; it need not resolve
later dependencies. An encountered dependency-resolution failure returns an
error.
The function observes the current state that the caller intends to inspect.
Freshness checking has a separate observation scope from criterion execution.
Checked observations enter the new trace when execution explicitly reads
or delivers them.
A checked snapshot can be reused if it still represents the current state.
